speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help me determine the cause, could you describe exactly where the pain is located and what it feels like? Also, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and have you noticed any blood in your urine or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome (IC/BPS).

The history of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, increased frequency, and recent dyspareunia in a 40-year-old female strongly points to IC/BPS. I have reached my diagnostic conclusion based on these key clinical features.
